Dangling-reference repairs:
- "Pragmatism represents a perfectly familiar attitude … than it has ever yet assumed.": referring words "as it seems to me" (the author's first-person stance). First-person cut, mid-sentence, so two quotes joined by `{}`.
- "But the general triumph of that method would mean an enormous change in … the 'temperament' of philosophy.": referring words "what I called in my last lecture" (first person, and it points outside the frame). First-person cut, mid-sentence, joined by `{}`. The cut words only point, so nothing outside the frame is left.
- "But they all own the corridor, and all must pass through it …": referring word "they" (the occupants of the rooms). Whole antecedent kept: the two sentences listing the rooms ("In one you may find …", "In a fourth …") stay in the note.

Other selection notes:

- "The universe has always appeared …": the quote starts after "So", whose only premise was the magic illustration. That illustration is dropped, and the first letter is capitalised.
- CAPS emphasis (CHANGED, PRINCIPLE, the THEORIES sentence, ANTI-INTELLECTUALIST, the ATTITUDE sentence, TRUTH) is copied as the file gives it.
